To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enhancement of cellular antioxidant-defence in diabetic cardiomyocytes preserves diastolic function by preventing RyR2 hyperphosphorylations, which in turn prevents the RyR2-leak and normalizes the [Zn2+i] and [Ca2+i] levels.
an enhancement of cellular antioxidant-defence in diabetics preserves diastolic function via regulation of both [Zn2+ ]i and [Ca 2+]i in the cardiac myocytes.
an enhancement of cellular antioxidant defence preserves diastolic function in hyperglycemia via regulation of both Zn2+ and RyR2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the novel mechanism underlying the preservation of diastolic function in hyperglycemic cardiomyocytes by an enhancement of cellular redox state.
a novel mechanism for the preservation of diastolic dysfunction by the modulation of both [Zn2+ and Ca+]i via RyR2 macomolecular-complex in hyperglycemic hearts.
a new mechanism of action of cellular antioxidant-defence in the treatment of diabetic cardiomyopathy and the role of both [Zn2+]/[Ca2+]i in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cellular antioxidant-defence augmentation in diabetics is an effective therapeutic strategy in preserving diastolic dysfunction and that it can be achieved via a modulation of RyR macromolecular-composite.
an enhancement of cellular antioxidant-defence in diabetic heart preserves diastolic function via regulation of both [Zn2+i] and [Ca2+i] and prevention of RyR2-leak.

an enhanced cellular antioxidant-defence in diabetic heart preserves diastolic Ca2+ and Zn2+ homeostasis via modulation of RyR macromolecular-complexe and thus prevents diabetes-induced diastolic dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a subcellulare oxidative stress marker can be activated if cells are exposed directly with Zn2+, which in turn can cause hyperphosphorylations in both RyR2 as PKA and Ca2+MkII.

the enhancement of cellular antioxidant-defence preserves diastolic function via regulation of both intracellular Zn2+ and intracellular free Ca2+ and prevention of RyR2-leak in hyperglycemic cardiomyocytes.

the cellular redox-state plays a pivotal role in the regulation of both Zn2+ and RyR2 macomolecular-complex in diabetics and the modulation of these processes by NAC treatment is likely responsible for the observed beneficial effects in diabetic rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enhancement of antioxidant-defence via directly targeting heart can preserve the diabetic cardiomyocytes from diastolic dysfunction.
the cellular antioxidant defence is an important target for the prevention of diabetic cardiomyopathy.
the cellular Zn2+ and RyR2 are the key targets in diabetic heart and that an antioxidant defence enhancement may be an effective strategy to treat diabetes-induced heart disease.
